extraction.name: ACL OCL
extraction.description: ACL OCL is a scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist open scientific research in the Computational Linguistics domain. It contributes metadata, PDF files, citation graphs, and additional structured full texts with sections, figures, and links to Semantic Scholar.
extraction.creator: Shaurya Rohatgi, Yanxia Qin, Benjamin Aw, Niranjana Unnithan, Min-Yen Kan
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data was collected by designing crawlers to fetch PDF documents and metadata from the ACL Anthology website. Files longer than 50 pages were removed. The PDFs were then processed for full-text extraction using GROBID and figure extraction using PDFFigures, and the data was enhanced using the Semantic Scholar Graph API.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: PDF files and metadata of scientific papers (conference, journal, and workshop papers) in the computational linguistics domain.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Pre-trained language model (PLM) for topic classification and a public language detection toolkit
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to peer-reviewed and open-access computational linguistics papers from the ACL Anthology, meaning it is not a comprehensive corpus. Additionally, the use of open-source PDF-to-text tools may limit text quality, and the corpus lacks annotations for specific tasks.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed to assist open scientific research in computational linguistics, benefit existing research tasks, and enable temporal topic trends analysis.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The maintainers plan to update the dataset annually to keep it synchronized with the ACL Anthology, with a long-term goal of hosting the data directly on the ACL Anthology via extraction APIs.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data preprocessing includes filtering out PDF files longer than 50 pages, extracting full text from the PDFs using the GROBID toolkit into a structured JSON format, and automatically detecting and adding language and topic fields.

name.evidence: We present ACL OCL, a scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist Open scientific research in the Computational Linguistics domain.

description.evidence: We present ACL OCL, a scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist Open scientific research in the Computational Linguistics domain. Integrating and enhancing the previous versions of the ACL Anthology, the ACL OCL contributes metadata, PDF files, citation graphs and additional structured full texts with sections, figures, and links to a large knowledge resource (Semantic Scholar).

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: The OCL corpus includes 73,285 papers hosted by the ACL Anthology [...] From the ACL Anthology, we design crawlers to fetch all the PDF documents and metadata from its website. [...] We then obtain 73,285 conference joumal and workshop papers in the CL domain.

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: The OCL corpus includes 73,285 papers hosted by the ACL Anthology published from 1952 to September 2022.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: We first train a pre-trained language model (PLM) based topic classification method on a subset of 2,545 scientific papers with ground truth topic labels. We then extrapolate and integrate the model predictions as silver-labeled topic information in the OCL. [...] To detect the language in which a document is written, we utilize a public language detection toolkit (Shuyo, 2010)

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: The OCL corpus is a small-scale collection of documents specifically focusing on peer-reviewed and open-access CL papers. As a result, it is not a comprehensive corpus like S2ORC... only open-source toolkits are considered, although it is acknowledged that some paid PDF2text services might yield higher-quality full texts... The OCL corpus is an unlabeled resource, lacking annotations for specific tasks that require labels.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We introduce ACL OCL, a scholarly corpus aiming to advance open research in the computational linguistics domain. The structured full texts, enriched metadata... can benefit existing research tasks as well as enable more opportunities. We highlight the utility of OCL in temporal topic trends analysis in the CL domain.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: In the future, we will work on the data currency of OCL, which aims to keep OCL up-to-date with the ACL Anthology data. We plan to update OCL by year to keep it alive. The ultimate solution is to provide full-text extraction and information extraction APIs to ACL Anthology, thus hosting the OCL data on ACL Anthology itself.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We remove PDF files longer than 50 pages, which are mostly conference volume introductions4 or handbooks. [...] we use GROBID7 for the full-text extraction from PDF files. [...] We add automatically detected fields such as language and topic to enable further analysis.
